Governor Adeleke of Osun State yesterday promised that a Commission of Inquiry will be constituted to investigate all reported killings and acts of violence connected with this election period after today’s governorship election.

The Governor expressed condolences to the families of all persons who have tragically lost their lives in incidents of violence during this election period at a press conference yesterday.

Adeleke who was represented by the Osun State commissioner for Information and strategies, Oluomo Kolapo Alimi said “Every life lost is an Osun life. Politics should never cost anyone his or her life, irrespective of political affiliation.”

IPCR: Let Ballot, Not Violence, Decide

The Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution (IPCR) has warned political actors in Osun State against allowing violence, intimidation and inflammatory rhetoric to overshadow Saturday’s governorship election, urging all stakeholders to ensure that the ballot, rather than coercion, determines the choice of the people.

The warning came yesterday, less than 24 hours before voters in the state are scheduled to elect their governor, amid heightened concerns over election-related violence and security threats in parts of the state. Recent security assessments have identified several Osun local government areas as vulnerable to electoral violence.

In an immediate press statement signed by its Director-General, Dr. Joseph Ochogwu, the IPCR charged governorship candidates, political parties, their supporters, security agencies, election officials and voters to place the interest of Osun above partisan considerations.

The Institute cautioned that political competition must not degenerate into violence, intimidation, threats, hate speech or destruction of property, stressing that political contests are temporary while the consequences of electoral violence could scar individuals, families and communities for years.

“Elections should not be treated as a do-or-die affair,” the Institute said, urging political leaders and candidates to demonstrate leadership by cautioning their supporters against inflammatory statements, misinformation and actions capable of escalating tensions.

The IPCR also delivered a clear message to candidates who may be dissatisfied with the outcome: accept the result peacefully or seek redress through the courts, rather than resorting to self-help.

It urged the candidates and political parties to respect the rules of democratic competition and demonstrate maturity before, during and after the election.

The Institute equally called on voters to resist attempts by politicians or other actors to recruit them as agents of violence, urging them to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and respect the rights of citizens supporting rival political parties.

It advised voters to maintain order at polling units, respect election officials and security personnel, and avoid confrontations with political opponents.

The IPCR further warned citizens against becoming conduits for election-related misinformation, particularly on social media, urging them to verify information before sharing rumours or unconfirmed reports capable of triggering unrest.

The appeal comes against a backdrop of heightened political tension in Osun, where reports of shootings, killings, clashes and other politically linked disturbances have fuelled concerns over the security of the August 15 poll.

Election Monitor Deploys iReportINEC

A civil group, the Tap Initiative for Citizens’ Development has appointed renowned Nigerian actress, activist and public voice, Kate Henshaw as Ambassador for iReportINEC, its citizen-led election monitoring and transparency platform designed to strengthen the reporting and documentation of electoral incidents across Nigeria.

This is coming as the civil group disclosed that iReportINEC is currently being deployed in Osun Governorship elections with over 20 percent of polling units covered so far.

The platform is expected to provide accurate and timely eye witness accounts in the already tensed situation in Osun State, over today’s governorship poll.

In a statement, Executive Director of Tap Initiative, Martin Obono, who observed that democracy does not end with casting a vote, stressed that citizens must also be able to see, document and demand accountability for what happens throughout the electoral process.

“For Tap Initiative, the message is simple: witness the vote, document what happens. Report responsibly, strengthen electoral accountability”, he said.

“Kate Henshaw brings public trust, civic consciousness and a strong commitment to citizen participation. Her voice will help us take iReportINEC to millions of Nigerians,” Obono added.

The statement also quoted Kate Henshaw as saying, “I am honoured to serve as Ambassador for iReportINEC. Democracy belongs to all of us, and our responsibility does not end when we cast our votes. Citizens must pay attention, document what they witness and demand accountability”, shortly after accepting her appointment.”

According to the newly appointed ambassador, “iReportINEC gives Nigerians an opportunity to become active witnesses to the electoral process. I am particularly excited about encouraging young Nigerians to take ownership of their democracy and use technology responsibly to protect the integrity of our elections.”

Kate Henshaw has consistently used her public platform to promote civic participation, voter engagement and accountability. Her own experience during the 2023 elections, when she publicly raised concerns about voter accreditation at her polling unit, further highlighted the importance of documenting citizens’ experiences during elections.

As Ambassador, she will support public awareness and encourage Nigerians, particularly young people, to use iReportINEC to document electoral incidents and contribute to credible election monitoring responsibly.

The platform is being positioned for the 2027 general elections, with a nationwide strategy covering Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Osun Speaker Expresses Worries Over Threats

The Speaker, Osun State House of Assembly, RT. Hon. Adewale Egbedun, yesterday decried disturbing reports of attacks, intimidation and threats against citizens and political actors in Odo Otin Local Government Area of Osun State in the past 48 hours.

According to him “The reports before us are deeply troubling. We have received accounts alleging that Armed Military personnel posted to Odo Otin Local Government led by Sikiru Adeboye have been moving through communities in Odo Otin, targeting leaders and members of the Accord political platform.

“This action must not be dismissed or politicised. They require immediate, independent and transparent investigation by the appropriate authorities. Among the incidents reported is an attack on the residence of an elderly woman, Alhaja Popoola Kuburat Ijadunola (popularly known as Mama Mi Leko), who happened to be an elder sister of former Governor Olagunsoye Oyinlola. Her residence was invaded and two of her children were taken away.

“There are also reports of attacks on Ayanyemi Joshua Olawale (Lawesco), Fasola Femi (Odofin) and Ajimoti Rasheed Omotayo (Action). Gunshots were fired and Mr. Ajimoti’s dog was killed.

“This is disturbing. No Nigerian citizen, regardless of political affiliation, age, social standing or location, should live in fear of armed personnel or believe that his or her home can be invaded with impunity. Of even greater concern is the release of three armed,” he alleged.

He called on the Department of State Services, Police, Nigerian Army and other relevant authorities to immediately investigate these allegations and make the findings public.

He equally called on the National Human Rights Commission, civil society organisations, election observers, diplomatic missions and credible international human-rights institutions to pay close attention to developments in Osun State and, where appropriate, independently document allegations of violations of citizens’ rights.

Civil Society Situation Room Deploys 70 Organisations

The Nigeria Civil Society Situation Room said it has deployed observers with over 70 Civil Society Organisations to monitor the election across the 30 Local Government Areas and 332 wards of the state.

The group noted that the Osun poll, being the last major election before the 2027 general elections, was a litmus test for the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, security agencies, and the political class.

According to the statement jointly signed by its Conveners, Y.Z Ya’u, Mma Odi and Celestine Odo, the Situation Room was worried by reports of politically motivated violence, clashes between supporters of political parties, attacks and intimidation, tension around motor parks and transport unions, allegations of thuggery, deaths and arrests of political actors.

It said the development was more troubling given that INEC identified 385 election flashpoints across the state, while its partners, Kimpact Development Initiative, KDI, and CLEEN Foundation, identified 13 LGAs as critical and high violence-risk areas.

It also condemned the recent attack on an INEC Permanent Voter Card, PVC, distribution centre in Odo-Otin LGA, where PVCs and BVAS devices were reportedly stolen, describing it as a sign of vulnerability of electoral infrastructure.

Oyintiloye: Competence, Credibility Not Material Inducements Will Determine Outcome

A chieftain of the APC, Hon. Olatunbosun Oyintiloye, yesterday said money, bread, rice and other material inducements will not determine the outcome of today’s governorship election in Osun State, stressing that competence and credibility will play a more decisive role.

Oyintiloye stated this while speaking with newsmen in Osogbo, Osun State, noting that while material inducements might temporarily influence some voters, they would not ultimately determine their choices at the polls.

He said Osun people are intellectually sophisticated, politically conscious and highly educated, adding that they are increasingly looking beyond temporary material benefits and are more concerned about the dividends of democracy that will improve their lives, benefit their children and advance the development of the entire state.

According to him, the people desire sound healthcare delivery, quality education at all levels, good road networks, employment opportunities, economic empowerment and inclusive governance.

“These are issues that directly affect their future, and I believe they will weigh them carefully when making their choices at the polls,” he said.

Oyintiloye noted that voters may accept money, rice, bread or other items offered by politicians, but stressed that accepting such materials does not necessarily translate into voting for the person who offered them.

He said the ballot remains personal, adding that voters can still make their final decisions based on their conscience and assessment of the candidates.

World.title: (Updated) Osun Election: 3,292 Polling Unit Results Uploaded on INEC IReV Portal
World.content:
A total of 3,292 polling unit results have been uploaded to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) IReV portal, representing 87.48 per cent of the 3,763 expected results in the ongoing Osun State election.

The figure was recorded as of 8:48pm on Saturday, August 15, 2026, as the electronic uploading of results from polling units continued.

The IReV portal provides a platform for the public to view polling unit results uploaded during elections, offering greater transparency in the results transmission process.

The number of uploaded results is expected to increase as more results from polling units across the state are uploaded.

World.title: INEC Materials Distroyed By Hoodlums as Voters Run for Safety in Ejigbo, ADC Candidate, Salaam, Reacts
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

At unit 13 ward 4 in Ejigbo local government area of Osun State, polling unit of the ADC governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Najeem Salaams was disrupted by political thugs as all INEC materials were destroyed completely.

Also voters at the polling unit ran away for their safety.

However, while reacting after the attack, ADC candidate, Dr Najeem Salaam, said “There was a total disruption of the electoral process and their plan was to attack me.

According to him, “That was an attempt to attack me personally. It was my strategic movement away from that area that made it impossible for them to attack me. Of course, my security personnel protected me and helped me get out of the area.”

“So, it is not a small thing; it is a big issue. This was a well-planned attack. And why did it happen immediately after I cast my vote? People had been voting before I arrived to cast my own vote. It happened immediately afterwards, and because of the strength I have in my unit, I did not just wait around.”

“I feel so bad and sad about it. I am worried and disturbed about the state of Nigerian democracy, the way we are going, and the way security operations are being handled. What does the future hold for everybody in this country?”

“It appears that when you belong to a particular party or have the backing of the government, you can do things the way you want. This is not fair. This is not democracy.”

“A lot of people ran for their lives. I wish you had the pictures and captions to show it. Elderly women and men ran away to save their lives. So, how can one be happy with this?”

“The citizens needed protection and assistance, but they were not getting the help they needed. It is worrisome and disturbing. That is it.”

“The security officials have arrested one of them, and I hope and believe he is still in their custody. We will pursue this afterwards because, in an attempt on my life, I cannot close my eyes, remain calm or stay silent about it. I will follow it up and escalate the matter.”

“Even after the election, the person needs to be questioned. Why was this done? Was it really targeted at me?”

” I can see that the Security Agencies were just looking. The security officers were just watching, and I think it is expected because they may be conniving with certain political parties.”

“They were just looking. That is why sometimes people take the law into their own hands and do things, and that is how we normally have crises in our society.”

“If we really want to protect the democracy that we are all yearning for, this is not the way to go.People are being denied. This is the use of force. I said somewhere, how can we differentiate this from military rule? When people vote and their votes do not count, what is all the preparation for? Why are we campaigning?”

“This is not an election; it is a selection. You want people who want to be in power, and then you select them. That is exactly what they are doing.”

“We appeal to whoever they are and whoever is listening to heed this call. This is not the way. You are in power today; you will not be there tomorrow. What legacy are we leaving for them,

Which direction are we giving to the people who are coming behind us?” Salam noted.

World.title: EU Observer Hub Reports 38 Security Incidents, 323 Electoral Offences
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The European Union Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria Election Observation Hub (EU-SDGN EOH) says it recorded 38 security incidents and 323 cases of electoral offences and irregularities in the 726 polling units monitored as of 12 noon on Saturday, as voting held in the Osun State off-cycle governorship election.

A preliminary statement issued this evening said, “the Hub, made up of the Centre for Media and Society (CEMESO), the International Press Centre (IPC), the Nigerian Women Trust Fund (NWTF), TAF Africa, The Kukah Centre (TKC) and Yiaga Africa, said it deployed 823 accredited observers across polling units in all 30 local government areas to monitor the election, which was contested by 15 candidates.”

“Of 2,339,233 registered voters, 1,906,390, representing 81.50 percent, had collected their Permanent Voters Cards and were eligible to vote, the Hub said.”

On the security incidents, the Hub reported 25 cases of thuggery, 12 attacks on electoral officials and 9 cases of voter intimidation by security personnel.

“It separately recorded 323 cases of electoral offences across the polling units observed, including 103 cases of vote trading, 85 cases of exposure of ballot papers, 31 cases of obstruction of voters, 38 cases of campaigning at polling units, 28 cases of inducement of polling and security officials, 14 cases of voter impersonation, 12 cases of multiple voting and 7 cases of misconduct by election officials.”

The Hub noted that the figures do not correspond to 323 individual polling units, as multiple offences were recorded at some locations.

The Hub also flagged specific cases of voter intimidation by security agents at PU 29-10-10-005, Igbon District Council School, Ejigbo, and PU 29-30-06-015, opposite No. 22 Oke Ola Street, Okanla Area, Osogbo.

“On the accreditation process, 608 of 726 observed polling units, or 83.7 percent, had polling officials with a full complement of both sensitive and non-sensitive materials between 7:30am and 8:00am. A further 75 polling units opened between 8:00am and 8:30am, and 42 between 8:30am and 11:00am, while one polling unit remained unopened as of 11:00am due to non-arrival of personnel and materials.”

The Hub said 58 Bimodal Voter Accreditation System devices malfunctioned in the polling units observed, of which 41 were subsequently fixed and accreditation resumed.

The Hub reported voter turnout as impressive, with women accounting for about 59 percent of turnout in observed polling units and more than 70 percent turnout among persons with disabilities at 12 designated PWD-friendly polling units. Women made up 36 percent of polling officials deployed.

The Hub’s fact-checkers said they had verified 11 false claims circulating about alleged payment of INEC officials, arrests by police and underage voting as of the time of the report, while claims relating to shooting and disruption of voting were still being verified.

The statement is a preliminary account covering the process up to 12 noon and will be followed by a full Post-Election Report after collation and declaration of results, the Hub said.

It urged political parties and candidates to pursue grievances through lawful and judicial channels in line with the Peace Accord signed on 30 July, and called for calm as the process moves toward conclusion.

World.title: Troops Thwart Another ISWAP Attempt to Overrun Military Base in Biu, Inflicting Casualties on Extremist Fighters
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja



Troops of 162 Amphibious Battalion, operating under the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, successfully thwarted an attempted attack by ISWAP terrorists on their location at Forward Operating Base Mandaragirau, Biu Local Government Area of Borno State, and inflicted heavy casualties on the extremist fighters, the military has said.

The military said the terrorists launched a simultaneous assault on the location from two fronts at about 0200 hours on 15 August 2026.

In a statement on Saturday, the Acting Military Information Officer of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, said that, upon detecting the advancing terrorists through emplaced early-warning and surveillance systems, a combat team was promptly dispatched to interdict the terrorists along one of their axes of advance.

“Contact was made, resulting in a heavy exchange of fire, during which the combat team decisively defeated the attackers on that front. The second group of terrorists attempted to bypass the ambush team and infiltrate the camp, but they were equally met with superior firepower and successfully defeated.

“The coordinated and aggressive response forced the insurgents to withdraw in confusion, after which troops immediately launched a hot pursuit and thoroughly exploited the contact area, as well as their withdrawal routes,” Captain Goni said.

The troops, he said, eliminated several terrorists and recovered a substantial quantity of equipment, comprising AK-47 rifles with loaded magazines, a rocket-propelled grenade launcher with bombs and chargers, one camcorder video camera and several other combat enablers, in a clear demonstration of tactical proficiency and combat dominance.

“Subsequent footage obtained from the surveillance systems further showed the terrorists dragging several bodies of their cohorts killed towards the Timbuktu Triangle. Notably, there were no casualties among our troops.

“The successful defeat of this multi-pronged attack further highlights the high state of readiness, aggressive posture and operational effectiveness of OPHK troops, with the additional impetus from the military high command,” the statement said.

The Theatre Command therefore commended the leadership, courage and professionalism of the troops of 162 Amphibious Battalion for their exceptional bravery and tactical excellence in decisively defeating the terrorists’ assault.

Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Goni said, remains resolute in its determination to dominate the battlespace, deny terrorists freedom of action, and restore lasting peace and security across the North-East.

World.title: WAPTV To Broadcast Blockbuster Indian Series, Rajjo
World.content:
Sunday Okobi

WAPTV, The Family Entertainment Channel, has reached another ground-breaking milestone, as it will be the first TV channel in Nigeria to broadcast the smash-hit Indian Romantic Drama, ‘Rajjo’.

The management of WAPTV said the move is an effort to ensure the TV channel maintains its apex position in providing premium programming for its millions of viewers worldwide, “in the ever-rising competitive world of broadcasting, as each TV Channel must stay on top of its game to keep eyeballs fixated on their screens.”

The show revolves around the trials and tests of an aspiring athlete, Rajjo, from Uttarakhand. Her mother, Manorama, has a dark past; hence, she is against Rajjo’s dreams of becoming an athlete.

Rajjo is a family drama, fully dubbed and subtitled in English.

The Director of WAPTV, Wale Adenuga Jnr, stated that “after years of painstakingly pursuing the broadcast licence of the hit show, ‘Rajjo’, we were delighted when we acquired the rights, as the series is tailor-fitted to our core values at WAPTV, to provide wholesome, family-friendly entertainment that will keep our audiences glued to their screens, both TV and Mobile.”

He stated Rajjo would start showing from September 7, 2026, Mondays to Fridays 10a.m. and Mondays to Fridays 9p.m. (repeat), Omnibus: Saturdays 10a.m., Sundays 7p.m. on WAPTV: DStv262, StarTimes 116, GOtv 129, FreeTV 751.

WAPTV can also be streamed worldwide via apps downloadable from the Google Play Store and Apple Store.

World.title: Sokoto Tasks Corps Members to Drive Local Devt
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Sokoto State Government has challenged members of the 2026 Batch B’ Stream 11 of the National Youth Service Corps posted to the state to position themselves as frontline agents of change in their host communities.

Governor Ahmed Aliyu gave the charge on Wednesday during the swearing-in ceremony that officially flagged off the three-week orientation course for the new batch at the NYSC Temporary Orientation Camp, Farfaru.

He was represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Alhaji Muhammad Bello Sifawa.

Addressing the corps members, the governor said their national service was more than a ceremonial rite of passage. According to him, it was a direct call to confront some of Nigeria’s most pressing problems with honesty, skill, and dedication.

“As a highly skilled segment of our population, it behoves on you to be part of the problem-solving team,” Aliyu declared. “Express your potentials through honest and dedicated service to your host communities.”

The governor did not mince words about the realities awaiting the corps members beyond the camp gates. He listed youth unemployment, poverty, rising crime, and a declining standard of living as “daunting developmental challenges” currently testing the country’s resolve.

Aliyu argued that such complex, multi-dimensional problems demand “every rationale means available to us,” stressing that corps members remain one of Nigeria’s most valuable human resources for grassroots transformation.

To succeed in their assignment, he advised the corps members to first seek to understand the people they are posted to serve. “Our people are generous and loving, but place high premium on respect for the law of the land, especially culture and ways of life generally,” the governor cautioned.

He also linked effective participation in camp activities to the broader goal of national development. According to him, drills, lectures, and skills acquisition programmes were carefully designed to put corps members “on the right perspective” for the tasks ahead.

Security concerns, a recurring worry for many deployed outside their home states, also featured in the governor’s address. Aliyu assured the gathering that the state government “is mindful of your welfare and security, and has provided significantly toward these.”

He further pledged that both the government and citizens of Sokoto would maintain a peaceful atmosphere to enable growth in the public and private sectors during the service year.

Earlier, the NYSC State Coordinator, Mr. Tyoyer Gabriel Ter, commended the new corps members for their conduct since arrival. He said they had “already exhibited positive virtues and high standard of patriotism” at the camp.

Ter charged them to embrace all camp activities, describing them as tools to build self-reliance and prepare youths for future responsibilities. He also expressed gratitude to Governor Aliyu and the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, for their consistent support for the scheme in the state.

The high point of the ceremony was the administration of the oath of allegiance by Justice Ibrahim Tambuwal, who represented the Chief Judge of Sokoto State, Justice Muhammad Saidu Sifawa. Hundreds of corps members clad in the scheme’s signature white and khaki, repeated the pledge to serve Nigeria with loyalty and integrity.

World.title: ‘You deserve it all’: Minister Gwarube spoils assistant with birthday goodies!
World.content:
On 12 August, Siviwe Gwarube, the Minister of Basic Education, pleasantly surprised her long-serving assistant, Shannon Malan, with birthday goodies.

MINISTER SIVIWE GWARUBE GIFTS ASSISTANT ON HER BIRTHDAY

The Instagram reel opens with the minister whispering into the camera, “I’ve got a surprise for the birthday girl. Come with me.”

She then walks down the office hallway with birthday goodies in hand. After entering Shannon’s office, the minister happily sings the birthday song and gives her the gift.



So, what was in the orange paper bag? The minister bought her a fancy kettle from Le Creuset, matching salt and pepper shakers, a balloon, and a handwritten card that reads, “Happy birthday. Thank you for all that you do for me. I love you.”

After receiving her birthday gift, Shannon said, “I love you so much, my ma’am. Thank you very much.”

MINISTER: ‘SHE RUNS MY LIFE’

In her birthday message to Shannon, the minister revealed they’ve been joined at the hip for almost a decade. Shannon started working as her assistant when she was the DA’s chief whip. However, managing her as a minister has proven to be quite challenging for Shannon.

“Shannon and I have been working together for 9 years. Almost a whole decade. She became my assistant when I was the Chief Whip of the Official Opposition. I’ve never looked back. But her most demanding and challenging job has to be managing *me* as a Minister,” she wrote.

The minister also praised Shannon for managing all facets of her life with the precision of a “Japanese train”, adding that even her family knows her.



“She runs my life like a Japanese train. Professionally and personally. My family knows her by name. My greatest achievements. They have been shared with her,” she added.

Lastly, the minister expressed deep gratitude for Shannon’s presence in her life, declaring she deserves all the spoils in the world.

“I’m so grateful for her. And any chance I get to spoil her, I’ll do it. As a reminder that she followed me to the edge of the cliff and jumped with me into the most uncertain and terrifying journey yet. Happy Birthday, my Love. You deserve it all!” she wrote.

World.title: ‘Voetsek!’: All Blacks supporters at Loftus put on blast
World.content:
All Blacks fans at Loftus. Images via Instagram

South African All Blacks supporters at Loftus Versfeld – where the New Zealand national team played the Bulls – were met with scathing remarks on social media.

The Kiwis won their third consecutive match in the Greatest Rivalry series, beating the Bulls 50-19.

The ABs have a large supporter base in South Africa, particularly in the Western Cape.



ALL BLACKS SUPPORTERS AT LOFTUS PUT ON BLAST

On social media, images and video clips of crowds of rugby fans at Loftus Stadium – some of whom were All Blacks supporters – had South African social media users riled up.

On the official Instagram account for the Greatest Rivalry Series, a group of locals held up a sign that read: “Adopt us. We’re South African, but our hearts are Kiwi”.

The post was captioned: “All Blacks fans are out in full force in Pretoria”

Outside New Zealand, the All Blacks have the strongest support in South Africa, particularly among the coloured community in the Western Cape. For many, the support is deep-rooted in Apartheid, when New Zealand stood with non-white players who were sidelined from joining the Springboks.

Under the post, the supporters were met with comments like…

“If you don’t support the country you live in, then go and live in the country you support”



“Voetsek, kindly then. Go well”

“Seriously? Go live in New Zealand”

“I’ve never seen white South Africans support All Blacks”

“Supporting the All Blacks is one thing. Holding up a sign saying your “heart isn’t South African” while living in South Africa is just embarrassing. Rivalry is fun. This is cringe”.

WHAT’S NEXT IN THE GREATEST RIVALRY SERIES?

The All Blacks have wrapped up three victories against the Stormers, Sharks and the Bulls.

They will take on the Lions next on 26 August at Ellis Park, Johannesburg.

New Zealand will also take on the Springboks in four test matches in the coming weeks.

World.title: Gayton McKenzie accused of another ‘insensitive’ post
World.content:
Gayton McKenzie has been criticised for two recent social media posts. Images via Facebook

Gayton McKenzie has been accused of making another “insensitive” post about a member of the Democratic Alliance.

The Patriotic Alliance leader – who is also the Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture – often uses his platform to call out the party helmed by Geordin Hill-Lewis, particularly over ward territory in the Western Cape.

Like the DA, the PA is also a part of the government of national unity (GNU),



GAYTON MCKENZIE ACCUSED OF AGEIST TWEET TOWARDS HELEN ZILLE

On his X account, Gayton McKenzie was accused of taking an ageist jab at Helen Zille, the DA’s mayoral candidate for Johannesburg.

The PA leader responded to a tweet that claimed that the was “two steps closer to Joburg mayorship”

Gayton responded: “She is one step closer to the graveyard at this age”.



In the comments section, many users found Gayton’s comment distasteful, particularly during Women’s Month. Others reminded the minister of his own past as a reformed convict.

@MrJLabuschagne: “Highly distasteful comment. You are losing traction and support because your ego is growing and your results aren’t keeping up”.

@IsoshalikaZulu: “Whatever your views are about @helenzille, this is distasteful language, especially coming from a sitting Minister. Be exemplary considering your past”



@Truter_Johan: “Tact clearly wasn’t part of the gangster-to-minister career development programme“.

She is one step closer to the graveyard at this age. https://t.co/sv7FRG7yoo — Gayton McKenzie (@GaytonMcK) August 13, 2026

MINISTER DELETES POST ABOUT DA MEMBER WHO DIED

A day later, after taking a jab at Helen Zille, Gayton McKenzie was criticised for making another social media post.



On Facebook, the PA president posted a picture of a DA-branded vehicle that had been involved in a car accident. The fatal crash claimed the life of DA activist, Mviki Ncapayi.

Without knowing about the fatality, Gayton warned DA members to “keep our names our your mouths”

Gayton – who shared “We are glad no one is injured” – also made a Biblical reference, adding “Touch not the anointed”.



The minister’s post was criticised by several DA members, including former PA MP Liam Jacobs, who labelled it “insensitive and fundamentally unsettling”.

Gayton responded on Facebook: “We deleted the post. The person in the bakkie passed away at the hospital, by the time I wrote the post, there have been no news of anyone injured. We sympathise with his family”

Chastising the DA for “lying” and “politicising the death of a man”, he added: “We can never rejoice in the death of anyone”.



He added, “Don’t throw stones when you live in a glass house. The war has started. We are ready to meet you at the ballot. You talk about PA, you will hear from us”

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs star dedicates Man of the Match award to ZCC
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs midfielder Siphesihle Ndlovu dedicated his Man of the Match award to the Zion Christian Church (ZCC) after producing a dominant display against Mamelodi Sundowns.

The Soweto giants held the Brazilians to a 1-1 draw at FNB Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Betway Premiership, with Ndlovu playing a key role in the result.

The hard-tackling midfielder marshalled the Kaizer Chiefs midfield and played a crucial part in their opening goal. Ndlovu held off the Sundowns pressure before setting up Langelihle Phili, who fired Chiefs into the lead in the 63rd minute.



His impressive performance was recognised after the final whistle when he was named Man of the Match.

Speaking after the game, Ndlovu dedicated the individual award to the ZCC, a church he is affiliated with.

“This means a lot to me. I want to dedicate this to the ZCC, where I come from. Jehovah is powerful,” Ndlovu said.  Kaizer Chiefs hold off Sundowns

The Chiefs midfielder also explained how a tactical adjustment helped Amakhosi find a way through against a Sundowns side that dominated possession for large periods of the match.

“It is never an easy match. Sundowns move the ball and make you shift from side to side. You have to be patient and wait for your moment. You are going to get it eventually,” Ndlovu told SABC Sport.

“I did what we needed to do, especially in the midfield.”



Kaizer Chiefs bossed the midfield

Ndlovu added that Amakhosi had to remain adaptable as Sundowns changed their approach throughout the match.

“It’s all tactical. If they change, we need to change. Obviously, we have good analysis. They see that and inform us on time, and we have to adapt quickly,” he explained.

The draw means Kaizer Chiefs remain top of the Betway Premiership standings with seven points from their opening three matches.



With Ndlovu emerging as one of the standout performers against Sundowns, his contribution could prove important as Chiefs look to maintain their strong start to the campaign.

Out of 10, how much do you rate Ndlovu’s performance?

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs transfer news: Cele, Zwane, Phili, CAF
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have been one of the teams to watch this season after making several impressive signings during the transfer window.

Amakhosi brought in Renaldo Leaner, Thabo Moloisane, Adolf Mtasingwa, Faiz Abrahams and Langelihle Phili as they looked to strengthen Fernando Da Cruz’s squad.

Three of the new signings have already made their debuts, with Phili standing out in particular. After being named Man of the Match in midweek, the 21-year-old winger scored his first goal in Chiefs colours during Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Mamelodi Sundowns.



Phili has quickly established himself as an important member of Da Cruz’s squad. In the three matches he has featured in, the youngster has shown plenty of quality and composure, suggesting that he could play a key role for Chiefs this season.

Kaizer Chiefs looking sharp this season

While Chiefs have strengthened their squad with new arrivals, several experienced players have also departed Naturena. Gaston Sirino and George Matlou are among those who have been offloaded.

Naledi Hlongwane, Samkelo Zwane and Bontle Molefe have also been sent out on loan to newly promoted Motsepe Foundation Championship side Hope FC.



Zwane, the oldest of the trio, has made only sporadic appearances since breaking into the Kaizer Chiefs first team. His previous loan spell at Siwelele failed to produce the desired results, and another temporary move could represent his final opportunity to prove himself at Amakhosi.

Another experienced player whose future at Naturena remains uncertain is Thabo Cele.

The 28-year-old midfielder has yet to feature under Da Cruz and does not appear to be part of the coach’s plans. With the transfer window still open, an exit now appears increasingly likely for the former Bafana Bafana international.



Should Cele stay for another season?

World.title: Derick Hougaard’s mom has a message for trolls
World.content:
The mother of Derick Hougaard has slammed trolls who have mocked the retired rugby player’s downfall. In recent weeks, the former Springbok and Bulls star, once dubbed the “Liefling van Loftus”, has made a public cry for help on his Facebook account.

The 43-year-old has suffered a series of personal setbacks over the years, including substance addiction, failed relationships and a series of health issues.

Recently, a GoFundMe campaign has been set up to help Derick cover everyday living expenses.



DERICK HOUGAARD’S MOM SLAMS TROLLS

On his Facebook account, Derick Hougaard’s last post is about his endorsement of a business and events listing app, Wha2do, created by Limpopo businessman Lesley Barnand

Under the post, one particular troll responded with a scathing comment that read: “He can’t even look at himself at his age, what else to say about an app. As soon as the first penny drops it’s straight to the bottle storage”.

The comment caught the attention of Derick’s mother, Riana Hougaard, who responded: “I pray for your heart”.



She continued: “Prayer carries power; we see it every day.

“The comments are shocking; they really reveal the state of people’s hearts”

Riana – who added that she was “exhausted” from the social media turmoil – thanked those who had shown her son love and support. 

“Appreciate all of you”, she added.

‘PRAY FOR HIS MIND’

It’s not the first time Derick Hougaard’s mother has addressed the public regarding her son’s well-being.

In 2023, after he was discharged from the hospital after a serious health scare, Riana Hougaard reposted a Facebook video of Afrikaans singer Chris Else, who had dedicated a song to the ailing athlete.



She shared: “God’s grace is great. So much power in prayer. Thank you again for your prayers and care, and love in this difficult time.

Riana hinted that both Derick’s body and mind needed to heal. She continued: “Please continue to pray for full recovery, strength, and for his mind. God carries us every day”.

Just weeks earlier, Derick Hougaard was found unresponsive in his Pretoria home by his then partner, singer Nadine.



According to Nadine, he had been found “suffocating.” He was rushed to the Steve Biko Academic Hospital, where he remained in a coma for three weeks until he awakened.

Derick was diagnosed with aspirational pneumonia; an infection doctors claim occurs when saliva, food, liquid, or vomit is inhaled or infiltrated into the lungs.

According to social media posts, Derick’s close friend Louis Liebenberg – who has since been imprisoned -stated that a mysterious bottle of liquid – presumed to be a cough mixture – was found in his possession. Liebenberg hinted that Derick had possibly been poisoned or had overdosed.



Speaking to Jacaranda’s Martin Bester, Nadine claims no alcohol or drugs were found in Derick’s system. She also claimed that Derick was not suicidal and did not overdose.

World.title: Upcoming Tuesday PowerBall jackpot crests R100 million
World.content:
It's good news for Tuesday PowerBall jackpot on 18 August 2026, with prize money cresting R100 million for the first time in months. Image: File

How much is the upcoming Tuesday PowerBall jackpot on 18 August 2026 worth? Well, following another round of rollovers this past Friday, R102 million is the total pot. The straight, non-cascading PowerBall is playing for R88 million. And PowerBall XTRA tags on an additional R14 million. Combined, this adds up to a R10 million bump over Friday’s winless roll …

Crucial to game mechanics for the 18 August 2026 Tuesday PowerBall jackpot is knowing how many rollovers have occurred since the last big payout. In the case of PowerBall, the last big win took place nearly six weeks ago, on Tuesday 3 July 2026, when R72 million paid out. Since then, twelve successive rollovers have occurred on PowerBall.

And PowerBall XTRA’s last cascade took place on Friday 31 July 2026. However, it was a relatively small one, and there have been four rollovers since then. The final PowerBall XTRA game of each month MUST payout (Friday 28 August 2026) no matter what. Players can only hope that the jackpot keeps climbing to a high-digit figure before it does …



TUESDAY POWERBALL JACKPOT ON 18 AUGUST 2026

Higher winnings typically means more players, which does increase the odds of a payout. Image: File

Nevertheless, there’s no trick to beat a random lotto draw. However, counting the number of rollovers does let you know when to play the game for the best odds of a split jackpot. New operator Sizekhaya doesn’t want massive winnings rolling over for more than one month. Therefore, being twice weekly, that equates to every eight games for PowerBall XTRA (but not outright PowerBall). Tuesday 18 August is game five of eight for the month.

Of course, every number combination carries identical odds, no matter if you choose an automated Quick Pick or the numbers manually. While neither approach shifts the underlying math, do remember that picking relatives’ birth days is less effective, because they only go to 31 instead of 50, for example.

PLAY TO WIN TUESDAY POWERBALL JACKPOT 18 AUGUST 2026

For first-time players, Tuesday PowerBall jackpot involves choosing five main numbers from 1 to 50, plus one PowerBall number drawn from 1 to 16. While PowerBall XTRA is an optional second draw using the same numbers entered in the main game. This comes for an extra fee, of course. Pricing has jumped since 1 June 2026. A standard PowerBall board now costs R10 and PowerBall XTRA costs R5 per board. Therefore, playing both together costs R15 total.

Tickets are sold at authorised National Lottery retailers. You can also enter via participating banking apps, including FNB, Capitec, Standard Bank, ABSA and Nedbank. The largest percentage of winners do come from the banking apps, purely due to the ease and convenience of the medium. However, note that some banking apps force a minimum purchase of two boards per ticket, effectively doubling the entry cost. Players must be 18 years of age or older to enter.

WHAT ARE THE ODDS OF WINNING TUESDAY POWERBALL JACKPOT?

The age-old debate of manual versus auto-generated picks does have some data behind it. Image: File

Here’s the good news, by shrinking the number pool, the jackpot odds for Tuesday PowerBall jackpot have improved from 1 in 42 million, to 1 in 33 million. And PowerBall XTRA carries identical odds to the main draw, since it uses the same number matrix. Of course, the big change to your odds is the cascading-jackpot rule.

R139 million was split three ways on Tuesday 30 June 2026 using this system. However, that’s still small potatoes compared with the record payout back in February 2019, when a Cape Town man collected R232 million after 24 consecutive rollovers. Under the new system we are not likely to see this sort of size again.



DRAW TIMES AND CLAIMING POWERBALL WINNINGS

PowerBall and PowerBall XTRA draw every Tuesday and Tuesday at 21:00. Sizekhaya brought back live televised draws using physical draw machines. Ticket sales cut off before the draw typically at 20:30, half an hour before the draw. All PowerBall prizes must be claimed within 365 days of the draw date. Anyone who misses that window forfeits their prize and the money is transferred to the National Lottery Distribution Trust for charitable causes.

How and where to claim Tuesday PowerBall jackpot winnings depends on the amount won:

Small prizes (up to R4 999 ) get paid out directly at licensed retailers.

) get paid out directly at licensed retailers. Mid-tier prizes ( R5 000 to R49 999 ) can be claimed at selected partner banks.

) can be claimed at selected partner banks. Online and banking-app players have prizes up to R249 999 deposited automatically into their accounts.

deposited automatically into their accounts. And anything above R49 999 (none banking app) requires an in-person visit to a Sizekhaya regional office, with the original ticket and a valid South African ID.

You can contact Sizekhaya to claim any old winnings, even from the ITHUBA era. Tickets are valid for 365 days. Image: File

Anyone unsure where to start can call the Sizekhaya helpline on 0861 026 000. Or you can visit one of the eight regional offices nationally:

And one final note, around R257 million in lottery prizes currently sits unclaimed across South Africa from the previous operator. Therefore, checking old ticket numbers against those drawn (up to one year ago) costs you nothing and might just turn up forgotten money. You can do so by clicking past results HERE.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs ‘R16 million’ signing scores his first goal
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs new signing Langelihle Phili get his first goal. Image: @KaizerChiefs/X

It seems Kaizer Chiefs’ ‘R16 million man’ has finally delivered for the Glamour Boys after much promise.

After three promising matches, Langelihle Phili scored his first goal for Amakhosi against Mamelodi Sundowns on Saturday afternoon.

Chiefs earned a draw at the FNB Stadium against their rivals to remain top of the Betway Premiership.



The winger opened the scoring in the second half after some excellent work from Siphesihle Ndlovu. Phili kept his composure to find the back of the net and put Chiefs ahead, although their lead did not last as Sundowns eventually found the equaliser.

Phili had been on Kaizer Chiefs’ radar during pre-season, with Stellenbosch FC initially placing a R16 million valuation on the talented attacker.

Rather than pay the full amount in cash, Chiefs negotiated a player-plus-cash deal to secure his services. Ashley Du Preez and Given Msimango were sent to Stellenbosch, alongside a reduced cash payment reportedly worth more than R5 million.

After showing plenty of promise in his opening matches, Phili finally announced himself on the scoresheet against one of the biggest teams in the country.

Kaizer Chiefs have already been eliminated from the MTN8 but still have three other cup competitions to compete in, including the CAF Confederation Cup, where Phili can shine.

With a goal in his fourth match, the former Stellies might be one of the players to watch this season.



Kaizer Chiefs made six signings this season

Thabo Moloisane got his first start since joining the club and also impressed at the back, keeping Mamelodi Sundowns attackers at bay. He is expected to play a big role this season, especially in the CAF Confederation Cup.

Did Phili impress?

World.title: ‘This is a big loss’ –  KZN MEC pays tribute to Scebi Dlamini
World.content:
UMSINGA - Friends, family, fellow Maskandi artists and fans laid artist Scebi Dlamini to rest.

The 29-year-old was being laid to rest in his hometown of Msinga, in KZN.

Dlamini died in a car crash in Richards Bay last Sunday, while on his way to perform at a festival. Dlamini died with Sipho "Gupta" Mchunu, his backup singer and stage crew member.

Mntomuhle Khawula, the Provincial MEC for Sports, Arts and Culture attended the funeral, he said the industry has lost one of its greatest.

“Indeed, the whole province of KZN, the country and the industry are grieving this big loss. The kind of talent that has come out of uMsinga is amazing. Condolences to the Mchunu and Dlamini families and to the whole area of uMsinga and uMzinyathi.”

World.title: ACDP promises clean governance and ‘new crop’ of leaders
World.content:
BENONI - The ACDP has launched its 2026 Local Government Elections Manifesto.

The party's outlined its plans ahead of the November polls.

Their leader Reverend Kenneth Meshoe said the party will bring a new crop of leaders focused on accountability and clean governance.

“Well, they have the right to lose hope with the current crop of leaders they have. But now with the ACDP, they will be having a different crop of individuals, people who are capable, and people who keep their weight.

“So a promise is that South Africa will not remain the same. If they put us in those offices, they elect our mayoral candidates, then they will see. They will ask themselves the question, why did we wait so long?” Meshoe said.

World.title: Reiger Park Shooting | “He was preparing for the future’ – Dimpane reflects on slain officer’s career
World.content:
REIGER PARK - Acting National Police Commissioner Puleng Dimpane described Anti-Gang Unit Constable Siphiwe Sibeko as a young officer dedicated to continuous learning and professional growth.

Sibeko was killed in Reiger Park last week.

At his funeral, Dimpane highlighted Sibeko’s extensive training during nearly seven years in the police service.

She said he was preparing for greater responsibility and the challenges ahead.

“These were not merely courses recorded on his personal file. They reflected a young police officer who understood that professional policing demands continuous learning discipline as well as preparedness.

“Significantly in May this year, only months before his death, Constable Sibeko successfully completed further maintenance shooting training in handgun as well as rifle. He was preparing himself for the future. He was sharpening his skills. He was maintaining his operational readiness. He was doing what a committed police officer does, preparing for the next call, the next shift and the next challenge,” Dimpane said.

World.title: ‘I imagined he’d sing at my wedding’ – fan mourns Scebi Dlamini’s passing
World.content:
UMSINGA - Fans remember Scebi Dlamini as a Maskandi superstar and a humble soul offstage.

Dlamini is being laid to rest in uMsinga, KwaZulu-Natal.

He died in a car crash last Sunday in Richards Bay, en route to a festival performance.

One fan said she loved Dlamini so much, she would have loved to have him perform at her wedding.

“I love the song Bengidakiwe because I always imagined that he would sing at my wedding. His music represented women,” she said.

Another fan said: “I have been a fan of Scebi since I started following Maskandi music. I admired his humility and it taught me the value of being loved for who you are. He brought us authentic, old-school Maskandi. His loss cuts deep.”

Dlamini’s death has also affected other fans in their personal lives.

“I learned of his death on Facebook that he had died, and my heart broke. For the entire week, I have been struggling to cope at work.”

World.title: Seven years on, Uyinene Mrwetyana remembered
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY – The Uyinene Mrwetyana Foundation held an awareness walk in remembrance of the slain UCT student.

Mrwetyana died aged 19 after she was raped and murdered by Post Office employee, Luyanda Botha in Cape Town.

Her death sparked outrage around the country after she had been missing for days before her body was found burnt and buried in a shallow grave in Khayelitsha.

Her mom, Noma, said her daughter's life must go beyond awareness.

She said Uyinene’s death should translate into concrete action to combat gender-based violence and femicide.

READ: Remembering Uyinene Mrwetyana

She called for a multidisciplinary approach involving different sectors of society and for stronger action against perpetrators of gender-based violence.

“Uyinene was killed on the 24th of August 2019 and this year is the seventh year. We commemorate her life and all other victims of gender-based violence today. We stand in solidarity with survivors of gender-based violence and femicide.

“We are here to put our heads together as a collective. Our theme says from awareness to action. We want more action on the ground and we ask for a multidisciplinary or multisectoral approach to the fight against gender-based violence," she said.

Former Miss Universe Zozibini Tunzi was one of the marchers and gave the keynote address said the fight against GBV needs a shift.

READ: WATCH | Five years since Uyinene Mrwetyana's murder

She said it should turn to effectively implementing existing policies and ensuring perpetrators are held accountable.

Tunzi said women are tired of raising awareness about gender-based violence and now want to see government take concrete action.

“Awareness is not a problem anymore; we've done more than enough of that. I think it is now time for the implementation of these policies that are supposed to be implemented correctly.

“I feel like we're not backed enough, we're not supported enough. We're seeing perpetrators get away with things every day, whether that be at the police station or whether that be at the high-end government level. Not enough is being done and that is exactly where the issue is,” Tunzi said.

World.title: Mourners celebrate the life of maskandi artist Scebi Dlamini
World.content:
UMSINGA – Fans, friends and industry peers have joined Scebi Dlamini’s family to say their last goodbyes to the much-loved maskandi star.

Dlamini, affectionately known as Inkosi Yama Gcokama, died in car crash last week.

Artists like Khuzani are at Umsinga where amabutho and traditional dancers are bidding him farewell.

The Kuyazenzakalela hitmaker has been described by many as humble and talented.

World.title: Reiger Park Shooting | Murder victim Roleen Lessing’s funeral underway
World.content:
REIGER PARK – Roleen Lessing was untimely killed in a shooting at the beginning of the month and today her loved ones are laying her to rest.

Lessing was one of two civilians who were killed in the Reiger Park shooting.

Two police officers attached to the Anti-Gang Unit who were responding to the shooting were subsequently ambushed and killed.

Lessing’s family and friends have ben joined by community members to bid her farewell.

World.title: Reiger Park Shooting | Constable Siphiwe Sibeko laid to rest in Springs
World.content:
SPRINGS – Family, friends and mourners have gathered in Springs to bid farewell to the slain Constable Siphiwe Sibeko.

Sibeko was one of the two Anti-Gang Unit members who was killed in Reiger Park earlier this month.

READ: Reiger Park Murders: Family defends accused gangster

The officer was ambushed together with a colleague while they were responding to a shooting incident in the area.

Four people died while a fifth was injured.

Today, Sibeko will receive a hero’s send-off and the police top brass in expected to be in attendance.
